speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you are experiencing postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness. To help narrow down the cause, how many weeks postpartum are you, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or unusual bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the prolonged labor and uterine tenderness are significant. Do you have any chills, or have you noticed any redness, warmth, or swelling around your incision or C-section site? (Note: You mentioned a vaginal delivery, but I need to confirm if there are any perineal lacerations or episiotomy issues). REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Urinalysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: While we await those labs, can you describe the character of your fever and whether you have experienced any nausea, vomiting, or a feeling of a distended, rigid abdomen? REQUEST IMAGINES: Abdominal_CXR_and_Pelvic_US.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (Endometritis) with possible secondary cystitis or urinary retention.
